The Brewers lead the World Series 1-0 and the Rays are near-even underdogs for Game 2, while Indiana visits Michigan a week after its first loss of the season. Here are the best prices on those games, Ole Miss vs Texas, UFC 333 and Maple Leafs vs Oilers. Saturday runs from a noon Big Ten kickoff in Ann Arbor to World Series Game 2 in Milwaukee, with a UFC title fight and Connor McDavid vs. Auston Matthews in between. The price that stands out most is Tampa Bay at +106 for Game 2, close to a coin flip with the Rays' ERA leader on the mound. Odds compare FanDuel, Fanatics, BetRivers, LetsBetMD (Maryland only) and DraftKings, were taken this morning, and all times are ET. Game 2 at American Family Field matches Drew Rasmussen for Tampa Bay against Logan Henderson for the Brewers. The regular-season numbers explain why Milwaukee is favored. The Brewers won 103 games with a +214 run differential, scoring 5.14 runs per game (second in MLB) and allowing 3.81 (fourth fewest). The 98-win Rays allowed 4.01 runs per game, sixth fewest, but their offense ranked 12th at 4.54. Rasmussen led the Tampa Bay staff with a 2.67 ERA, 16 wins and 174 strikeouts. The Rays are without Shane McClanahan, ruled out for the postseason with a forearm issue. The market prices Milwaukee at -120 to -127, roughly the value of home field plus a series lead. That leaves the Rays as the side with value: a near-even price on a team sending its best starter to the mound in a game it badly needs. The total of 6.5 looks fair with two run-preventing staffs, so it is a pass. The risk to the Rays is the Brewers' lineup, which outscored all but one team in baseball this season. Statistics Indiana Vs Michigan Odds: Spread, Moneyline And Total No. 6 Indiana (6-1) arrives in Ann Arbor after a 19-15 loss to Ohio State, while Michigan (4-2) is coming off a 21-18 win over Penn State. The Hoosiers average 36.6 points and allow 12.9; the Wolverines score 22.7 and allow 16.2, and Michigan gives up only 89.7 rushing yards per game. The spread has climbed from 6.5 earlier in the week to 7.5 everywhere, and BetRivers now hangs 8. That move looks like the market leaning hard on Indiana's season-long scoring average. The total tells a different story: five of Michigan's six games have finished under 42.5, and Indiana's last two games produced 37 and 34 points. A low-scoring, field-position game suits Michigan's defense, and that is where the value sits. The moneyline is not a serious option at -294 or shorter. Statistics Ole Miss Vs Texas Odds: Spread, Moneyline And Total Ole Miss (5-1) visits Texas (4-2) after a 31-3 win over Missouri. The Longhorns have lost two straight, both by 27-24, to Oklahoma and Florida. The Rebels average 37.5 points behind Trinidad Chambliss, who has thrown for 1,676 yards with 14 touchdowns and four interceptions. Texas allows 17.8 points per game, and edge rusher Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks. Texas is -149 to -164 on the moneyline and a field-goal favorite. DraftKings has Ole Miss +3 at -108 and BetRivers +3 at -109, FanDuel moves to +3.5 at a steep -122, and LetsBetMD is down at +2.5 at +100. The best moneyline on the Rebels is +132 at BetRivers. The market looks to be paying for the Texas name more than the Texas offense. The full three points matter in a game this tight, so the half-point at FanDuel is not worth the juice. Bet to consider: Ole Miss +3 at -108 at DraftKings. The more productive offense is getting points, and a loss by exactly a field goal still pushes. The co-main event is the bantamweight title trilogy between Petr Yan (20-5) and Merab Dvalishvili (21-5). This is a true pick'em: FanDuel has both fighters at -108, DraftKings both at -110 and BetRivers both at -112. Fanatics and LetsBetMD do not have the fight posted. The line has barely moved all week, which says the market has no strong opinion. A zero in the loss column is a big number, but the champion has 32 pro fights of experience against Evloev's 20. I'd take the champion at even money and keep the stake small. Bet to consider: Volkanovski moneyline -108 at FanDuel. The main risk is the obvious one: an undefeated challenger who has never been solved. Maple Leafs Vs Oilers Odds: Moneyline, Puck Line And Total Edmonton (8-1-1) leads the Western Conference and the NHL in scoring at 4.6 goals per game, with McDavid at 31 points (eight goals, 23 assists) in 10 games. The Oilers' power play is second at 35.3%, but their penalty kill ranks 23rd at 72.4%. Toronto (6-4-2) has won three straight, most recently 5-4 over the Rangers, and has the NHL's best penalty kill (97.4%) and third-best power play (28.6%). Matthews has 18 points. Tristan Jarry starts for Edmonton with Devon Levi on injured reserve, and defenseman Mattias Ekholm is out. Jarry has an .873 save percentage in three games. Toronto is without John Tavares and Chris Tanev. The Over 6.5 is the price that jumps off the board. Most books charge -147 to -152, while LetsBetMD has it at -111. With the league's top offense, a backup-quality save percentage in the Edmonton net and two top-three power plays, that gap is too big to ignore. The Leafs at +155 at BetRivers are a fair small-stakes alternative.
